E1.evidence: Issue #276 gives a reproducer ("ros2 run demo_nodes_cpp talker" in one terminal; "sudo timedatectl set-ntp no" and "sudo date -s @`date +%s | xargs -I@ echo @-5 | bc`" in another), an strace showing "FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET_PRIVATE|FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME", and a gdb stack through "dds_waitset_wait_impl ... rmw_wait () from ... librmw_cyclonedds_cpp.so". Cyclone maintainer confirmed: "the implementation of the timeout in `rmw_wait` (which is simply passed on to Cyclone's `dds_waitset_wait`) is using the wall clock rather than a monotonic clock." https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/276

E2.evidence: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp implements rmw_wait by forwarding a relative timeout to Cyclone's C API: "const dds_return_t ntrig = dds_waitset_wait(ws->waitseth, ws->trigs.data(), ws->trigs.size(), timeout);" (rmw_node.cpp at 45179db5). Cyclone converts it to an absolute wall-clock deadline: "const dds_time_t tnow = dds_time ();" / "const dds_time_t abstimeout = (DDS_INFINITY - reltimeout <= tnow) ? DDS_NEVER : (tnow + reltimeout);" (dds_waitset.c at af7aba56), where dds_time is documented as "Get the current time in nanoseconds since the UNIX Epoch." The rmw layer's contract states the clock expected for this wait: "Elapsed time should be measured using a monotonic clock, though rmw implementations could use a different one." (rmw.h). The failure depends on this clock assumption across the rmw_cyclonedds/cyclonedds boundary and the wrong timing (a late return from dds_waitset_wait) crosses it; the resolving edit is inside cyclonedds. Separate units: rmw_cyclonedds (ros2/rmw_cyclonedds) and the Cyclone DDS C library (eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds) are separately built and released.

E3.evidence: PAIR: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp passes the wait timeout into cyclonedds' dds_waitset_wait and consumes its return time; the failure is observed in that call path (gdb stack: dds_waitset_wait_impl <- rmw_wait <- rcl_wait <- rclcpp::Executor::wait_for_work).

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "once system time jumps back in 5 seconds, timer will be in sleep in 5 more seconds."

The resolution does not change rmw_cyclonedds, so the resolved revision is the broken one; note that a 2021 rmw_cyclonedds is unlikely to build against 2025 Cyclone master.

The reporter's gdb stack shows the same code path ("dds_waitset_wait_impl (... abstimeout=1611042784228497624) at .../cyclonedds/src/core/ddsc/src/dds_waitset.c:79"), consistent with this snapshot, whose dds_waitset_wait computes a wall-clock absolute timeout. Resolved: PR #2255 'Gracefully handle time jumps' was rebase-merged into master on 2025-08-05; 49c313a4 is its merge_commit_sha (last commit of the series on master).

failed_conditions.quote: Just to be sure: the issue you're running into is that implementation of the timeout in `rmw_wait` (which is simply passed on to Cyclone's `dds_waitset_wait`) is using the wall clock rather than a monotonic clock. Correct?

loudness_evidence: The delay is observed only as missing timer output and in strace/gdb, with no diagnostic from any tool: "once system time jumps back in 5 seconds, timer will be in sleep in 5 more seconds."

resolution.summary: Cyclone DDS associates its condition variables with a clock and implements relative waits on the elapsed (monotonic) clock: dds_waitset_wait now computes "const ddsrt_etime_t abstimeout = ddsrt_etime_add_duration (ddsrt_time_elapsed (), reltimeout);" instead of adding the timeout to dds_time(). No change in rmw_cyclonedds.
resolution.evidence: cyclonedds PR #2255 body: "The main commit in this PR allows blocking with timeouts based on a monotonic clock rather than the system clock. This should address the various problems with time jumps people have been facing. I haven't actually tested it with time jumps yet because of some practicalities" and "Fixes #1995 https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/276". Merged 2025-08-05; no report in the sources shows rmw_cyclonedds running with the fixed Cyclone across a time jump.

notes: The composition chosen is rmw_cyclonedds_cpp -> cyclonedds because the maintainers located the defect there (clalancette: "Is the problem here in `rmw_cyclonedds`, or in CycloneDDS itself?"; fujitatomoya: "with current implementation, this is because of [cyclonedds]") and the fix is in cyclonedds. The same wrong timing propagates one layer up through the rmw API to rcl/rclcpp (rcl_wait -> rmw_wait), where rmw.h states the clock attribute ("Elapsed time should be measured using a monotonic clock, though rmw implementations could use a different one."); fujitatomoya: "rmw suggests monotonic, but not a requirement." That rcl -> rmw_cyclonedds_cpp composition (element api:rmw_wait) is the same failure seen from the client library. Failure class 'other' was used because the mismatch is the clock against which a relative timeout is measured (wall clock vs. monotonic), which fits none of the listed classes; it is not a unit or encoding difference in the value itself. Related: ros2/ros2#1080 (same symptom with other rmw implementations, attributed there to libstdc++ condition variables) and cyclonedds #1995 ('Event thread is freezed when time is changed to past'). fujitatomoya reports the defect still present on Humble / Ubuntu 22.04 (2022-04-28). The issue was closed on 2022-09-30 before any fix existed; eboasson later described a local workaround (switching Cyclone's clocks to CLOCK_BOOTTIME). Inventory is limited to the Cyclone API functions rmw_cyclonedds uses around waiting and timing (the full set of used Cyclone APIs is much larger).
